बॉलीवुड में जिसे सबने फ्लॉप माना, उसी फिल्म ने बॉक्स ऑफिस पर 3000 करोड़ से ज्यादा कमाकर इतिहास रच दिया! 🎬

हिंदुस्तान टाइम्स लीडरशिप समिट 2026 में मेकर्स और स्टार्स पर बात करते हुए डायरेक्टर Imtiaz Ali ने Sonal Kalra से खास बातचीत की। 🔥

Imtiaz Ali ने बताया कि जब Dhurandhar बन रही थी, तब इंडस्ट्री के कई लोगों ने इसे सबसे अनप्रैक्टिकल और फ्लॉप होने वाली फिल्म कहा था। 😮

Aditya Dhar के डायरेक्शन और Ranveer Singh स्टारर इस स्पाय थ्रिलर ने सभी नियम तोड़ते हुए दुनियाभर में 3000 करोड़ रुपये से ज्यादा की कमाई कर ली।

मार्च में आई Dhurandhar: The Revenge ने एक दिन में 100 करोड़ कमाने का रिकॉर्ड बनाया और कुल 1720 करोड़ कमाए, हालांकि मेकर्स का दावा है कि वर्ल्डवाइड कमाई 1760 करोड़ से ज्यादा है। 💣

दिसंबर में रिलीज हुए पहले पार्ट ने भारत में 841 करोड़ नेट और दुनियाभर में 1308 करोड़ का कलेक्शन किया था।

क्या आपने Ranveer Singh की फिल्म Dhurandhar देखी है? आपको यह कैसी लगी, कमेंट्स में बताइए! 👇

ctx.title: At HTLS, Imtiaz Ali hails Dhurandhar, says many in Bollywood called it an impractical film, least likely to succeed
ctx.summary: Dhurandhar starred Ranveer Singh in the lead role and released in theatres last year in December. It went on to become a blockbuster.
ctx.text:
Writer-director Imtiaz Ali was one the speakers on the 24th edition of the Hindustan Times Leadership Summit 2026, where he spoke at length about the changing landscape of the Hindi film industry. The filmmaker, whose last release Main Vaapas Aaunga went on to become a surprise hit at the box office, picked the example of Dhurandhar and praised the film's daring to break many rules.
During his conversation with Sonal Kalra, Chief Managing Editor, Entertainment and Lifestyle, Hindustan Times at the 24th Hindustan Times Leadership Summit, Imtiaz said, “I feel something very interesting is happening in the film industry. We are in that delicious phase where people are saying that nothing is working. Should we go with the big star, non-star… what is going to work? People are saying that attention span is missing in the audience but the films which are doing well are three hours long. nothing long is working. People are citing Dhurandhar as an example of what is successful but look at the length of that film!”
He added, “Forgetting the fact that when Dhurandhar was actually conceived and it was doing its run around those studios, people thought that this is the most impractical, a film with the least likelihood of success! But it broke all the rules and after that everybody wants to make that. All of us are thinking what will work. The language might change but I feel its a phase of introspection that the film industry is going through.”
Aditya Dhar's two Dhurandhar films have grossed over ₹ 3000 crore at the box office. Released in December, the first Dhurandhar film, starring Ranveer Singh , was a critical and commercial success. It collected a then-record ₹ 841 crore net in India, and courtesy of a $33 million overseas haul, crossed ₹ 1300 crore gross worldwide. After a rather long run in theatres that lasted over 14 weeks, Dhurandhar ended its run at ₹ 1308 crore.
The sequel, Dhurandhar: The Revenge, arrived in March and shattered every Bollywood box-office record. The film became the first from Hindi cinema to net ₹ 100 crore in a single day, a feat it achieved three times during its opening weekend. It sailed past ₹ 1000 crore in a week and soon surpassed its predecessor. As of April 16, Dhurandhar 2 has earned just over ₹ 1025 crore net in India and ₹ 1720 crore worldwide. The makers claim the worldwide gross exceeds ₹ 1760 crore. Either way, the Dhurandhar franchise has crossed ₹ 3000 crore worldwide, with the upper estimate at ₹ 3110 crore for the two films.
Written and directed by Aditya Dhar, Dhurandhar is a spy thriller starring Ranveer Singh as an Indian spy infiltrating the gangs and terror networks of Pakistan. The films also star R Madhavan, Akshaye Khanna, Arjun Rampal, Sanjay Dutt, Rakesh Bedi, and Sara Arjun. The first part was critically acclaimed, while the second received more lukewarm reviews. However, both are the two highest-grossing Hindi films in India.
Santanu Das is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times with over 5 years of experience, writing on films, pop culture and film festivals. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several film festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. He also brings a sharp perspective to the monthly column called The Fault in Our Stars, where he writes about a recent film/series and what stops the ‘good’ from becoming ‘great’.

A gold medalist from Banaras Hindu University, Santanu completed his postgraduate studies in English from Jadavpur University. He is also a Rotten Tomatoes-certified film critic. When not watching films or speaking to celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique. His favourite books include The Corrections, The God of Small Things and A Room of One's Own.
